title: Module 6 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

o: There is no effect or no difference in the population
The treatment works
The sample mean equals the population mean exactly
The alpha level is zero
items.why: The null is the claim we test against. It says any difference is due to sampling error.

o: There is an effect or difference in the population
The null is true
The sample is biased
The p value is large
items.why: It is the research claim. We never prove it. We decide whether the data are inconsistent with the null.

o: The probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis that the researcher is willing to accept
The probability the null is true
The size of the effect
The sample size
items.why: Alpha is set before the study. A common value is .05.

o: Sample outcomes so unlikely under the null that we reject it
The most likely outcomes under the null
All possible sample means
The area in the middle of the distribution
items.why: If the test statistic lands in the critical region, the result is statistically significant.

items.q: A Type I error occurs when
o: The null is true and we reject it
The null is false and we fail to reject it
The null is false and we reject it
The null is true and we retain it
items.why: A false alarm. Its probability equals alpha when the null is true.

items.q: A Type II error occurs when
o: The null is false and we fail to reject it
The null is true and we reject it
We use the wrong test
Alpha is too small
items.why: A miss. Its probability is beta.

o: The probability of rejecting the null when it is false
The probability of a Type I error
The size of the effect
Alpha minus beta
items.why: Power equals 1 minus beta. Researchers aim for about .80.

o: The size of an effect in standard deviation units
Whether the result is significant
The probability of the null
The sample size
items.why: It is a mean difference divided by a standard deviation. Benchmarks of .2, .5, and .8 are conventionally small, medium, and large.

items.q: A 95 percent confidence interval for a mean is
o: A range of plausible values for the population mean
The range containing 95 percent of the scores
The range containing 95 percent of the sample means
A guarantee the mean is inside
items.why: It is built from the sample mean and its standard error, and it expresses uncertainty about the parameter.

o: The probability of results at least this extreme if the null were true
The probability the null is true
The probability the result will replicate
The size of the effect
items.why: It is a statement about the data given the null, not about the null given the data.
